title: docs(releases): the 17.2.0 and 17.3.0 upgrade checklists, written from a measured upgrade
body:
Fixes #15322

Pass 2 of a two-pass card, and the last one. Pass 1 landed as PR #15333 and is on `main`; this branch builds on it and does not re-touch anything it wrote.

**Baseline shas, both read from `origin/main` at worktree creation:**

| | sha | what it is |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| pass 1's merge | `19be9dfcd` | `docs(releases): 17.2.0 and 17.3.0 detail sections, and repair the upgrade entry page (#15322) (#15333)` |
| this branch's base | `dc46c4ec1` | `origin/main` tip at `git worktree add`; `19be9dfcd` verified an ancestor of it |

## What this delivers

The card's remaining half: the two Upgrade checklists on `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx`, and the **structural** documentation defects in `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` that two checklist tables could not have repaired.

The spine is a real upgrade of an application repository across one minor, driven as a customer: the reader was allowed the docs site, the `CHANGELOG.md` inside each published npm tarball, and the `os` CLI's own output, and nothing else. Its headline reading was that the documentation covered **zero** of the eleven breakages that run hit.

### `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx`

- `## Upgrade checklist` gains `### 17.2.0` and `### 17.3.0`; pass 1's interim paragraph (the one that sent readers to the per-change Migration notes instead) is deleted.
- The section lead is now a provenance frame rather than a promise of completeness.
- Two operational hard requirements are written in as steps, because skipping either one breaks a deployment: deduplicating autonumber columns **before** the new unique indexes can build on an existing database (the driver neither fails the boot nor skips silently — it logs on the `error` channel, and the constraint is simply not enforced until you act), and `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` on walled deployments, without which `AuthPlugin.init()` refuses to start.
- The dev-admin lockout (#15337) is written as a **known issue** with no workaround, not as a step, and with no prediction about which release might carry a remedy. It says what is affected, what the symptom is, that no workaround was found, and where to follow along.

### `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` — the four structural defects

| Defect | What the page now says |
| :--- | :--- |
| **1** — no npm/dependency upgrade path at all | New **"Moving the dependency pins"**: the shape `create-objectstack` scaffolds had no documented upgrade action, only a Docker tag and a systemd artifact swap. Three steps — bump every `@objectstack/*` pin as one set (including `devDependencies`, because `@objectstack/cli` is the binary that runs the author-time rules), regenerate and commit the lockfile, and check `specVersion` / `engines.protocol`, which move only at a major boundary. |
| **5** — "same major means move the tag and restart" | New **"A runtime move can still force metadata edits"**, narrowed by measurement rather than by assertion: `os validate` and `os build` refused a stack that compiled on the previous release, a lint family widened from 0 findings to 429, and an inert declared constraint started being enforced. The two-halves table at the top no longer answers the metadata question with a bare "no". |
| **6** — `os migrate meta` saying "Nothing to migrate" reads as "you are done" | The limit is now stated **next to the command**, in the section about what the command does not do. It is scoped to the protocol chain and silent about author-time rules, lint families, flipped defaults and newly-enforced constraints — measured, it printed that line and exited 0 while **nine** separate changes were live on that stack. |
| **7** — the per-package `CHANGELOG.md` files are authorised only for v10/v11 | New **"The per-package changelogs are the exhaustive record"**. I picked *point every upgrader at them* over *compile them into the release page*, and said why on the page: the release pages are deliberately triaged (17.3.0 alone carries 862 entries), so compiling everything would destroy the property that makes them readable, while the changelogs already ship inside every tarball the reader has installed. The two are complementary, and the page now says which question each answers. |

The v17.3.0 / v17.2.0 rows in the per-release table repoint from the Migration-note anchors to the new checklists.

## The scope fact this PR is built around

⛔ **The drill measured one hop: 17.2.0 → 17.3.0.** The card was filed believing the app was pinned at 17.1.0 and crossing two minors; that premise was corrected on the card, and I did not build on it. **Nobody has walked 17.1.0 → 17.2.0.**

So the two lists are kept apart, and the page says so in as many words:

- **17.3.0** — every line marked **measured** was walked on the real upgrade using published artifacts only. Several of those lines are changes whose own changelog entries are *not* marked breaking (`delete ctx.input.field` becoming real, the undeclared-key refusal, unknown flow functions, the widened i18n family), which is exactly why a checklist is not a restatement of the breaking-changes section. Lines that the run did not reach — the SDK namespace rename, the record-share backfill, the loud permission-store failure — are marked **not exercised** and cite the change's own Migration note.
- **17.2.0** — the whole list is marked **not exercised**, with a warning at the top of it: accurate about what changed, unproven about what it costs to cross.

A step nobody has run, presented beside steps that were, is how a reader finishes a checklist and believes they are done — which is the exact harm the drill recorded under its sixth documentation defect.

## Transcript drift

Four pages printed `Running author-time rules (41)...`; the registry resolves **42** (`AUTHORING_RULES` has 42 entries, 39 declaring `ALL` and 3 declaring `['validate', 'build']`, so `authoringRulesFor('validate').length` is 42 — matching what the CLI printed on the measured run). The drill named two of the four pages; leaving the other two stale would have left the identical claim in place, so all four moved. **Number only** — no surrounding prose was touched, and no new gate was built here. Nothing currently reads these transcripts, which is filed back to the PM as an out-of-scope finding rather than fixed in this card.

## Gate readings — actual numbers

All **42** runnable gate commands were derived at the final commit `1207c1312` by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` (the script reads the change set from the merge base itself; it is not fed a hand-made file list). Each ran with its output redirected to a file **before** the exit code was captured, so no pipe could rewrite a status. **41 of 42 exit 0.**

The two the card asked for by name:

```
✅ check-doc-anchors --self-test: slug parity, custom ids, duplicate counters,
   extraction discrimination and both finding classes verified (305 live fragment links)
✅ check-doc-anchors: 305 internal #fragment link(s) across 410 source file(s)
   all resolve to a real heading
```

```
node scripts/check-release-section-coverage.mjs             exit 0   (the PR-blocking form)
node scripts/check-release-section-coverage.mjs --self-test exit 0
node scripts/check-release-section-coverage.mjs --strict    exit 1   1 finding — see below
```

305 fragment links is up from the 302 pass 1 measured, and the gate resolves cross-file fragments, so it is what proves the six new inbound anchors land — `#1720` and `#1730` from the per-release table, plus `#moving-the-dependency-pins`, `#a-runtime-move-can-still-force-metadata-edits`, `#the-loop` and `#what-it-does-not-do--read-the-output`.

**The single non-zero is pre-existing and inherited, measured on both trees rather than argued.** A detached compare worktree at base `dc46c4ec1` reports `exit 1`, **1 finding**; this branch reports `exit 1`, **1 finding**, with byte-identical text. Both name `content/docs/releases/index.mdx` — a file this diff does not touch, because its repair is a separate card (#15332) already dispatched to another seat. The compare worktree was removed after the measurement. Only `release-coverage-patrol.yml:203` passes `--strict`; the PR-blocking invocation at `lint.yml:2729` is the non-strict form, which exits 0 here.

⚠️ One honest non-reading: running `check-doc-anchors.mjs` in that compare worktree answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` / exit 3 (`github-slugger` is not installed in a fresh worktree). **That measured nothing** and is reported as neither a pass nor a failure; the branch's own green above stands on its own.

## Changeset

None, deliberately. The diff publishes nothing from any package — it is six files under `content/docs/` — so this wants the `skip-changeset` label, which the PM applies. ⛔ Not an empty changeset: an empty frontmatter file is rejected, and an all-empty set stalls the release silently.

## Guardrail note

`content/docs/releases/` is release-owned and must never be a rider on a code PR. This is the guardrail's own escape hatch, used as written — a **dedicated docs-only PR**, no code, no drive-by edits — and it is the vehicle the card was filed to use.
